card.name: Verbs and links in all-caps warnings
card.fires_on: Short function or helper words (HAS, HAVE, BE, SO, GIVEN) and word endings (DO-SE) inside warning text written entirely in capital letters. It fires where the all-caps sentence continues into a verb such as BEEN or a connector.

modes.label: Helper verb after subject
modes.description: HAS or HAVE right after a condition or event in a capitalized warning, before BEEN reported or observed.
modes.example: AN IMMUNE MEDIATED HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA<< HAS>> BEEN OBSERVED IN PATIENTS RECE

modes.label: Connector or split word
modes.description: The word SO or the start of BECAUSE inside a capitalized instruction or caution.
modes.example: PROMETHAZINE HYDROCHLORIDE SHOULD NOT BE USED IN PEDIATRIC PATIENTS LESS THAN 2 YEARS OF AGE<< BE>>CAUSE OF THE POTENTIAL FOR F

card.writes: It suppresses capitalized logic words like NOT, ALL, ONLY and AND, so it seems to damp the next all-caps connector.
card.plain: It lights up on small linking words in warning paragraphs typed in all capitals.
